verdict.summary: Since the developer-platform changes (effective November 17, 2025), an OAuth app that serves users outside your own team or organization has to be published as a public app and pass Figma review, which states 5–10 business days but has run a month or more in 2026. Even after approval, View and Collab seat users get roughly 20 Tier-1 calls (GET file, nodes, images) per month, and Figma's hosted MCP server rejects normal OAuth apps entirely, with new MCP clients paused.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Draft apps can be tested by you and your plan admins without review.

timeToProd.assumes: A public OAuth app reading file content (file_content:read) for any Figma user; a private app for your own team or organization publishes the same day with no review.
timeToProd.waitingOn: Figma's public-app review (stated 5–10 business days on the submission page; community reports of 4+ weeks in 2026).

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Figma's docs give no official SLA. The 5–10 day figure is quoted by a developer from the submission page; month-long waits are community reports acknowledged by staff as 'in line for review'.

prerequisites.item: A Figma team or organization to own the app
prerequisites.why: Every OAuth app must name a team or organization as owner; end users don't need to belong to it.

prerequisites.item: Registered redirect URLs and browser-based (not WebView) authorization
prerequisites.why: Token exchange only works with registered redirect URLs, and WebView access to the OAuth flow isn't supported.

prerequisites.item: For a public app: testing instructions, test credentials or trial access, optionally a video
prerequisites.why: Reviewers need to exercise the app against the Community Apps Review Guidelines.

prerequisites.item: Users with Dev or Full seats if your agent reads files often
prerequisites.why: View and Collab seats are capped at up to 20 Tier-1 requests per month, which covers GET file and GET file nodes.

scopeTiers.impact: Published directly with no review, but only usable by users in the owning team or organization. Good for internal agents, not for a product.
Any Figma user can authorize after Figma approves the app. Scope additions need re-review (community reports of 'scope update pending review').

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Scope-change re-review is inferred from forum thread titles, not docs.

scopeTiers.impact: Only work for users on Enterprise plans; org:* scopes also need an organization admin and some need Governance+.
Being removed; apps had to migrate to granular scopes when re-publishing.
Limited to clients in the Figma MCP Catalog; a normal OAuth app client ID/secret won't grant it, and staff said in August 2026 that adding new MCP clients is paused.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Catalog restriction is in the scopes doc; the pause is a staff forum statement.

steps.title: Pick scopes and the app type
steps.detail: Map each REST endpoint you call to a granular scope (e.g. GET /v1/files/:key needs file_content:read). Decide private (team/org only) vs public (review).

steps.title: Create the OAuth app
steps.detail: In My apps, create an app, choose the owning team or organization, and copy the client secret immediately (it's shown once). The app starts in draft.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Console page resolved (HTTP 200); we didn't sign in.

steps.title: Configure redirect URLs and scopes
steps.detail: Add redirect URLs and tick the scopes in the app's OAuth credentials and settings.

steps.title: Implement the authorization code flow
steps.detail: Redirect to https://www.figma.com/oauth?client_id=...&redirect_uri=...&scope=...&state=...&response_type=code (PKCE recommended). Exchange within 30 seconds at POST https://api.figma.com/v1/oauth/token with HTTP Basic client auth.

steps.title: Implement refresh
steps.detail: Access tokens expire after 90 days by default. Refresh at POST https://api.figma.com/v1/oauth/refresh; the refresh token is reusable, but each refresh invalidates the previous access token.

steps.title: Test as a draft app
steps.detail: Authorize with your own account (only you and plan admins can use a draft app).

steps.title: Design around seat-based rate limits
steps.detail: Cache file JSON, prefer GET file nodes for subsets, and detect View/Collab users, who get up to 20 Tier-1 calls per month. Limits are per user, per plan, per app.

steps.title: Prepare review materials
steps.detail: Draft testing instructions, a scope-by-scope justification and reviewer notes; set up test credentials or trial access to your service.

steps.title: Record a test video (optional) and publish as public
steps.detail: Choose public in publishing settings and submit for review with the testing materials.

steps.title: Figma review
steps.detail: Figma emails approval or requested changes. No official SLA; the submission page reportedly says 5–10 business days, and developers reported month-long waits in spring 2026.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: Community thread; staff confirmed submissions were queued but gave no timeline.

steps.title: Go live
steps.detail: Once approved, any Figma user can authorize. Keep scopes stable, since adding scopes appears to need another review.

agentCanDo: Implement OAuth with PKCE, the 30-second code exchange and refresh
Build caching and seat-aware rate limiting
Draft reviewer testing instructions and scope justifications
Check OIDC discovery for Sign in with Figma
humanMustDo: Sign in and create the app under a team or organization
Copy the client secret when it's first shown
Provide reviewer test credentials or trial access
Submit the public app and answer reviewer feedback
Apply to Figma (or your account team) if you need MCP access

blockers.symptom: Users outside your team get an error authorizing, or only you can use the app
blockers.cause: The app is still a draft (only you and plan admins) or private (only team/org users).
blockers.fix: Publish as a public app and pass Figma review.

blockers.symptom: An older app suddenly can't call the REST API
blockers.cause: Apps created before September 23, 2025 that weren't re-published by November 17, 2025 moved to draft.
blockers.fix: Migrate off files:read to granular scopes and re-publish (public apps go through review).

blockers.symptom: 429s after a handful of GET file calls for some users
blockers.cause: View and Collab seats get up to 20 Tier-1 requests per month, and limits may drop under high demand.
blockers.fix: Cache aggressively, use node-level requests, and tell users a Dev or Full seat raises limits.

blockers.symptom: Token exchange fails with an invalid or expired code
blockers.cause: Authorization codes expire 30 seconds after issue, or redirect_uri differs between steps.
blockers.fix: Exchange immediately server-side and send the identical redirect_uri.

blockers.symptom: Your agent can't connect to mcp.figma.com with its OAuth app
blockers.cause: mcp:connect is limited to MCP Catalog clients, and new client onboarding was paused as of August 2026.
blockers.fix: Use the REST API with your OAuth app, or submit the MCP client request form; Organization/Enterprise customers can ask their account team about private clients.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Pause comes from a staff forum post.

blockers.symptom: Public app review sits for weeks with no response
blockers.cause: Review backlog; Figma gives no official SLA.
blockers.fix: Ask on the Figma forum to have it flagged, and keep testing instructions clear so it isn't bounced.

nuances.text: Figma keeps one access token per app per user: refreshing invalidates the previous access token, so concurrent workers must share token state. The refresh token itself is reusable.
Scopes don't override org, team, folder or file permissions; a token only sees what the user can see.
Figma has standard OIDC (issuer https://www.figma.com, scopes openid/profile/email, ES256) for sign-in, separate from the REST API scopes.
Figma's MCP authorization server advertises dynamic client registration (api.figma.com/v1/oauth/mcp/register), but per staff that doesn't grant access unless the client is catalog-approved.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: Metadata fetched on 2026-10-20; we didn't attempt registration.

nuances.text: Figma for Government uses a separate token endpoint (api.figma-gov.com).
